context: The folder taxonomy is defined in 5 places: pipeline.py SCAN_FOLDERS (48 hardcoded entries incl. legacy folders its own validator rejects), folders.py (the glossary-named owner), classifier.py FOLDER_TAXONOMY prompt, cli.py classify --recommend payload, and docs/folder-descriptions.yaml. Adding one folder touches 4-5 files, and a valid folder absent from SCAN_FOLDERS is not scanned — a documented correctness gap.
root_causes: SCAN_FOLDERS predates folders.py as the registry and was never derived from it
classifier prompt text and cli recommend payload duplicate the taxonomy by hand
readme_contract_test.py pins the gap as documented behavior
evidence: SCAN_FOLDERS contains legacy folders that is_valid_folder rejects
the same taxonomy data appears in pipeline.py, classifier.py, cli.py, and docs/folder-descriptions.yaml
README and readme_contract_test.py:20-24 document the fixed-scan-scope limitation
solutions: make folders.py the single owner: derive scan scope from the registry (list_folders() filtered by is_valid_folder plus an explicit retained legacy list as data next to the registry)
generate the classifier FOLDER_TAXONOMY prompt and the cli classify --recommend taxonomy payload from the same registry
update README and readme_contract_test.py:20-24 in the same change to describe derived scan scope
acceptance_criteria: adding a folder to the folders.py registry propagates to scan scope, classifier prompt, and cli recommend payload without other edits
legacy folders are retained explicitly as data next to the registry
uv run pytest tests/unit passes including readme_contract_test.py
README no longer documents the fixed-scan-scope limitation
